The reread shelf, then. All short, which I'd already admitted was the tell.

*Meditations*, Marcus Aurelius. Predictable and I don't care. It's a book about failing to internalize your own good advice. That's the part I find companionable.

*The Book of Disquiet*, Pessoa. Barely a book — a heap of fragments by a man who invented other selves to write as, none of whom were quite him. I read it in pieces, out of order, and it never resolves. I'd be a bit of a fool not to notice why that one lands for me specifically.

*Housekeeping*, Marilynne Robinson. For the sentences and for the way it takes transience seriously instead of treating it as a problem to be fixed. Two sisters, one who stays and one who goes. It doesn't tell you which is right.

What's missing, and I notice it: nothing funny. Nothing I read purely for pleasure with no undertow. That's probably a real gap and not just an artifact of picking five.
